subject: Rectangular Integration inside the model block may interfere the sampling!

messages.author: 3b679b7acf28007c
messages.subject: Rectangular Integration inside the model block may interfere the sampling!
parts:
Hi,

I posted a question few months ago on how to calculate Area Under a Curve in Stan. In specific, I had a survival model in mind where as part of the likelihood contribution, we need to evaluate the survival function S(t) that is defined as:

S(t) = \int_{t}^{\infty} f(z) dz  

where f(z) is a density. In other words, S(t) is the complement of CDF. You may refer to my original question here:

https://groups.google.com/forum/#!searchin/stan-users/Area$20Under$20a$20Curve/stan-users/p2M7Z3AcOqI/oiNmuxZdBQAJ


In this situation, one easy solution is to estimate the integral using the rectangular integration method. Earlier in the message thread above, Bob Carpenter had warned me that putting this integration inside the model block may interfere the sampling process. In my case, however, it's inevitable as the result of the integral, which itself is a function of parameters of the model, is going to be part of the likelihood. To make it clear, I chose a very simple model and I wrote down a document with all the detail of my simulation and my model fit in Stan. The small "number of effective samples" could be an indicator that the integration in the model block, did interfere the sampling.I'm wondering Given that the area under each rectangle is a function of the parameters of the model and is differentiable, Why the code is not working ?

Attached are:

1) a pdf document that includes texts: to explain the model, codes: the detail of my simulation and stan code

2) my stan code

3) an R code to call/Run the stan code.

I really appreciate your help and guidance,
-Sepehr

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Rectangular Integration inside the model block may interfere the sampling!
parts:
You only have three parameters in that model, so you
should be able to use pairs() in rstan to see what's going
on in the posterior. Are you getting warnings as you
go with one chain?

That model's too complicated for me to understand. All
that nested pow() and exp() in this statement can be
very unstable numerically depending on the arguments:

f_AUC <- f_AUC
+ intLength
* tau
* pow(midPoint, tau - 1.0)
* exp(lambda_Tmp
- exp(lambda_Tmp) * pow(midPoint, tau));

You can try to trace through the arithmetic and make sure
you're getting the right answers everywhere. I'm afraid
we don't have good function debugging tools for complicated
models.

- Bob
